headline: Run DeepSeek Locally for $5, Not $5K
summary: DeepSeek's new optimization lets developers run powerful AI models on consumer GPUs. No enterprise hardware needed — just smart quantization and memory management.

slides.title: Why Pay $5,000 for Local AI?
slides.subtitle: Run DeepSeek on a $5 consumer GPU instead.
slides.body: Most engineers assume local LLMs need enterprise GPUs. DeepSeek proves otherwise — what changed?
slides.deep_dive: Running large language models locally has historically required VRAM-heavy cards like A100s or H100s, pricing out individual developers. DeepSeek's new release introduces aggressive quantization and memory offloading that shrinks model footprint by 90%+ without catastrophic quality loss. This isn't just compression — it's a rethink of how attention and KV-cache are managed during inference, letting a 7B parameter model run in 4GB VRAM.
slides.key_fact: DeepSeek now runs on sub-$100 GPUs with 4GB VRAM.
slides.why_it_matters: Democratizes local AI development — no cloud costs, no data privacy tradeoffs.

slides.title: DeepSeek Local Inference Engine
slides.subtitle: Quantized weights, KV-cache streaming, CPU offload.
slides.body: Loads 7B-70B models on consumer cards. Integrates with Ollama, llama.cpp, and custom Python pipelines.
slides.deep_dive: The toolchain provides pre-quantized GGUF/EXL2 weights for DeepSeek-Coder and DeepSeek-Chat variants. It auto-detects GPU VRAM, splits layers across GPU/CPU, and streams KV-cache to system RAM when VRAM fills. Supports dynamic batching for throughput. No Docker, no Kubernetes — single binary or pip install. Works on Linux, macOS (Metal), Windows (DirectML).
slides.why_it_matters: Drop-in replacement for cloud APIs in dev loops, CI, and air-gapped environments.

slides.title: How It Fits 70B Params in 8GB VRAM
slides.subtitle: Layer-wise offload + KV-cache streaming + 4-bit quantization.
slides.body: Model splits across GPU/CPU. Only active layers stay in VRAM. Rest streams from RAM.
slides.deep_dive: Traditional inference loads all weights into VRAM. DeepSeek's engine uses a layer-swap scheduler: at each forward pass, only the current transformer block's weights occupy GPU memory. Previous block's weights are evicted to CPU RAM; next block's weights are prefetched asynchronously. Meanwhile, KV-cache (which grows with context length) is compressed via 8-bit quantization and offloaded to system RAM, fetched per-token. This turns VRAM from a capacity constraint into a bandwidth pipeline.
slides.key_fact: VRAM usage stays flat regardless of model size — only context length grows RAM usage.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables 70B models on 8GB cards; 7B on 4GB cards.

slides.title: Editor → Local Agent → Code Index → DeepSeek Engine
slides.subtitle: Local-first AI coding loop with zero cloud hops.
slides.body: Your IDE talks to a local agent that indexes code, queries DeepSeek, returns diffs.
slides.deep_dive: The architecture eliminates network round-trips. A lightweight agent (Rust/Go) runs as a language server plugin. It maintains a semantic code index (Tree-sitter AST + embeddings) in SQLite. On query, it retrieves relevant context, constructs a prompt, calls the local DeepSeek engine via Unix socket, parses structured output (diff/JSON), and applies edits via LSP. All components are single-process or local IPC — no HTTP, no auth tokens.
slides.key_fact: End-to-end latency: 200-800ms for code gen on RTX 3060.
slides.why_it_matters: Feels like Copilot but runs entirely on your laptop — even offline.

slides.title: Developer Query → Structured Artifact
slides.subtitle: Natural language in, verified code diff out.
slides.body: Input: task + context. Processing: retrieval + inference. Output: parseable diff.
slides.deep_dive: The workflow mirrors a compiler pipeline but for intent. Developer types "add retry logic to fetchUser". Agent retrieves fetchUser definition, call sites, error types. Constructs few-shot prompt with project conventions. DeepSeek generates unified diff. Agent validates diff applies cleanly, runs type-check (if configured), presents as inline suggestion. No free-form chat — every output is a machine-verifiable artifact.
slides.key_fact: Output schema: unified diff + test plan + risk assessment.
slides.why_it_matters: Turns LLMs from chatbots into reliable code transformers.

slides.title: Don't Treat It Like Cloud API
slides.subtitle: Context window ≠ VRAM. Quantization has limits.
slides.body: Mistake: stuffing 100K tokens. Fix: retrieve only what's needed. Mistake: expecting GPT-4 quality. Fix: use for scoped tasks.
slides.deep_dive: Common antipatterns: (1) Disabling retrieval to 'see everything' — floods context, evicts KV-cache to RAM, kills latency. (2) Running 70B on 8GB for chat — works but 2 tok/s. Right-size model to task: 7B for edits, 34B for architecture. (3) Ignoring quantization drift — 4-bit loses nuance in complex reasoning. Calibrate with your eval set. (4) Skipping dry-run — local models hallucinate imports. Always validate before apply.
slides.key_fact: Retrieval quality > context length for code tasks.
slides.why_it_matters: Avoids slow, wrong outputs. Keeps the 'local Copilot' feel snappy.
items: Use semantic retrieval, not full-file context
Match model size to task: 7B edits, 34B design
Calibrate 4-bit on your codebase eval set
Always dry-run diffs — local models hallucinate imports
Pin KV-cache to RAM, not swap — use mlock()

slides.title: Run DeepSeek Locally in 3 Commands
slides.subtitle: From zero to local AI coding in 5 minutes.
slides.body: Install engine, pull model, connect IDE. No Docker, no cloud account.
slides.deep_dive: The onboarding is intentionally minimal. `pip install deepseek-engine` pulls the inference binary with Metal/CUDA/DirectML wheels. `deepseek pull deepseek-coder:7b-4bit` downloads ~4GB GGUF. `deepseek serve` starts the Unix socket. VS Code extension auto-detects. JetBrains plugin uses same protocol. Config lives in ~/.deepseek/config.toml — set VRAM limit, quantization, retrieval depth. First query indexes your workspace (one-time).
slides.why_it_matters: Removes every friction point between you and local AI.
takeaways: pip install deepseek-engine && deepseek pull deepseek-coder:7b-4bit
deepseek serve → install VS Code/JetBrains extension
Set VRAM limit in ~/.deepseek/config.toml to leave headroom for OS
